notes: Identity independently verified from supplied canonical text: full primary research article, Learning About What Others Were Doing: Verb Aspect and Attributions of Mundane and Criminal Intent for Past Actions, William Hart and Dolores Albarracín, Psychological Science 22(2), 261–266, DOI 10.1177/0956797610395393. Printed publication year 2011, online 30 December 2010, explains reference-year difference. Article includes all three experiments, discussion, notes and references. No PDF was supplied, so no rendering performed. Study 3 and article p. 4 identify the source section but do not distinguish its two intentionality outcomes. Candidate 1: criminal intentionality, printed d = 0.76, F(1, 46) = 7.02, p = .01 (equality). Candidate 2: Mind Attribution Scale intention attributions, printed d = 0.66, F(1, 46) = 5.29, p = .03 (equality). These are separate tests; no metrics converted and no target selected by numerical matching. The detailed-processing measure (d = 0.73, p = .02) is a distinct process outcome and was not selected. Candidate participant count 48 is stated in Experiment 3 methods, not explicitly labelled final analytic N; it is retained for parent field-scope review only. No group-count arithmetic or df-based N inference. All positive values remain candidates pending outcome identification. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
